observations.epoch_band_state_and_other_notes: FL Cet = SDSS J015543.40+002807.2; exact Gaia DR3 counterpart. Catalog distance uses Bailer-Jones geometric posterior median 317.594 pc; legacy 319 pc and Schmidt+05 model distance ~290 pc retained as alternatives in audit. Orbital-period value is ODonoghue+06 eclipse ephemeris; competing Schmidt+05 value remains separate. Barrett+20 X-band I=11±5 uJy (2.2 sigma by I/error) is a marginal reported signal, not an upper limit; Ridder+23 excludes it below 3 sigma. Distinct WD Zeeman/cyclotron fields and model caveats are in rawdog_measurements.csv.

issues.parameter: white dwarf magnetic field / field geometry
issues.competing_evidence: Inight+25 low-state photospheric Zeeman spectrum: offset-dipole fit Bpole=50–58 MG, Hα sigma components B>=33 MG; high-state cyclotron humps ~23 MG. Schmidt+05: low-state main cyclotron spot 29 MG and possible high-state ~48 MG second spot, explicitly not definitive. These diagnose different regions and states; the Inight field fit is model-dependent and cursorily explored.
issues.why_it_matters: A single collapsed magnetic-field value would conflate photospheric/polar and cyclotron-emission-region measurements and bias comparisons of WD magnetic fields across populations.
issues.needed_action: Keep all diagnostics separately typed as saved. For a unique field geometry/mean surface field, obtain an independent phase-resolved Zeeman/cyclotron reanalysis with broader offset-dipole parameter exploration and radiative-transfer treatment; no single scalar is presently preferred.

issues.competing_evidence: Schmidt+05 Table 2: 0.06051621(4) d; O’Donoghue+06 Eq. 1: 0.0605163312(7) d, formally separated by 0.01047 s per cycle (~3.0 combined formal sigma). Wiehahn+04 gives 87.1435±0.0002 min, consistent with O’Donoghue within its larger error; Woudt+04 photometric value is much less precise. O’Donoghue et al. describe their ephemeris as consistent with earlier values and note intrinsic timing scatter.
issues.why_it_matters: The adopted orbital clock and any inferred period change affect phase predictions and evolutionary timing; a formal discrepancy should not be erased by averaging.
issues.needed_action: Check later published eclipse timings or collect new timings and fit a common ephemeris including possible period derivative and timing noise; until then retain the O’Donoghue ephemeris as catalog scalar with all competing values attached.

issues.competing_evidence: Barrett+20 reports X-band Stokes I=11±5 uJy, circular polarization +100±53%, positional offset 0.17±0.25 arcsec and custom total S/N=6.6. Simple I/error=2.2; Ridder+23 excludes FL Cet from its >=3 sigma luminosity sample. The radio-derived ~3.56 kG ECM field is conditional and does not identify the emitter as the WD.
issues.why_it_matters: Treating a marginal point as a secure detection or a WD field would distort radio-population comparisons and emission-mechanism interpretation.
issues.needed_action: Reinspect image-level Stokes maps/noise and obtain repeat or independent radio data to verify the signal and its polarization; until then retain the value as a reported marginal signal with no upper-limit substitution.
